items.title: systemctl: manage services
items.description: Start, stop, enable at boot and check status.

items.title: systemctl: inspect
items.description: Find failed units and see what is running.

items.title: journalctl: read logs
items.body:
journalctl -u {{service}} -f
journalctl -u {{service}} --since "1 hour ago"
journalctl -p err -b                 # errors since this boot
journalctl -n 100 --no-pager
journalctl --disk-usage
sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=7d
items.description: Filter by unit, time and priority.

items.title: Disk space checks
items.body:
df -h                          # per filesystem
df -i                          # inode usage
du -sh /var/* | sort -h        # biggest directories
lsblk                          # block devices
sudo find / -xdev -type f -size +500M 2>/dev/null
items.description: Find what is using the disk.

items.title: Memory and CPU checks
items.body:
free -h
uptime                         # load averages
nproc
vmstat 1 5
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head
top -o %MEM
items.description: Quick health check.

items.title: Create a swap file
items.body:
sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
swapon --show
items.description: Add 2 GB of swap on a small server.

items.title: Add a user and give sudo
items.description: Create an account and add it to the sudo group (Debian/Ubuntu).

items.title: Users and groups: common tasks
items.description: Modify, lock and remove accounts.

items.title: Safe sudoers editing
items.body:
sudo visudo
# or a drop-in file:  sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/deploy
# example line:  deploy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /bin/systemctl restart myapp
items.description: Always use visudo, which validates syntax.

items.title: Harden SSH
items.body:
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
# test the config, then:
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
items.description: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config, then reload (keep a second session open).

items.title: ufw firewall basics
items.body:
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw default allow outgoing
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw status numbered
items.description: Default deny incoming, allow what you need.

items.title: ufw: manage rules
items.body:
sudo ufw delete {{rule_number}}
sudo ufw allow from 203.0.113.5 to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw deny 3306
sudo ufw reload
sudo ufw reset
items.description: Delete rules, restrict by source and reset.

items.title: iptables: list rules
items.body:
sudo iptables -L -n -v --line-numbers
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
items.description: Show current rules with counters.

items.title: iptables: basic web server rules
items.body:
sudo iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -P INPUT DROP
items.description: Allow loopback, established traffic, SSH and web; drop the rest. Run from a console, not only over SSH.

items.title: iptables: save and delete
items.description: Persist rules and remove one by number.

items.title: Time, hostname and system info
items.body:
timedatectl
sudo timedatectl set-timezone Europe/London
hostnamectl
uname -a
cat /etc/os-release
lscpu | head
items.description: Identify the machine.

items.title: Who is logged in and recent logins
items.body:
who
w
last -n 20
lastb -n 20          # failed logins (needs sudo)
items.description: Auditing basics.

items.title: Find and stop a runaway process
items.body:
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -5
kill {{pid}}          # SIGTERM (polite)
kill -9 {{pid}}       # SIGKILL (last resort)
items.description: Identify the heavy process, then terminate it.

items.title: logrotate config example
items.body:
/var/log/myapp/*.log {
    daily
    rotate 14
    compress
    delaycompress
    missingok
    notifempty
    copytruncate
}
items.description: File: /etc/logrotate.d/myapp.

items.title: systemd timer (cron alternative)
items.body:
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/backup.sh

# /etc/systemd/system/backup.timer
[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=true
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

# enable: sudo systemctl enable --now backup.timer
items.description: A service plus a timer unit.

items.title: File permission audit
items.body:
sudo find / -xdev -perm -0002 -type f 2>/dev/null       # world-writable files
sudo find / -xdev -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null       # setuid binaries
ls -ld /etc/shadow
items.description: Find risky permissions.
